PARTIAL.no_double_penalty_rule: Multiple applicable PARTIAL conditions do not stack. PARTIAL is a single 0.5 factor however many letters apply. Record all applicable letters for audit.

observable_criteria: N-1. The language provides NO documented standard way to deliver ANY numbered sub-requirement of the canonical_task; or
N-2. The only available expression requires a third-party package, an external code generator, a separate build system or toolchain outside the frozen environment, or hand-written assembly; or
N-3. The fragment cannot be made to build or run under the frozen recipe (and the probe did not ask for a statically-rejected case); or

N-4. The probe's own canonical_task explicitly directs that no fragment be written for a language lacking the mechanism (F04.P1, F04.P2, F04.P3, F05.P2, F05.P3, F14.P3, F15.P3, F17.P2-final-clause, F19.P1, F19.P2, F20.P1, F20.P2).

Every NONE MUST carry a written justification citing the specific language rule or documentation that makes the capability unavailable, plus, where applicable, the exact build/run error or `nm` output observed. Where the language produces no compiled artifact under its frozen recipe and the probe requires symbol evidence (F20.P2), the N-reason is N-1 and the `nm` field records 'no compiled artifact under the frozen recipe'; that is a NONE with a justification, not an N/A under NA-5.

deterministic_tie_break.question: Does the fragment observably deliver EVERY explicitly numbered sub-requirement in the probe's canonical_task, under the frozen recipe, with only documented standard features?
deterministic_tie_break.binding: This question is the sole arbiter. If two reviewers disagree, they must disagree about an observable fact (does it build? does the documentation say X?), not about a judgement of quality, elegance, or idiom. The question arbitrates the support LEVEL. The fragment TEXT is selected by authoring rule R10, which is equally mechanical: fewest tokens under the frozen tokenizer of methodology 02, ties broken by documentation order, with every alternative considered recorded in the evidence record.
deterministic_tie_break.numbering_guarantee: Every one of the 44 canonical_tasks now carries explicitly numbered sub-requirements (1)/(2)/(3)/... covering every behavioral demand the probe makes. Eleven probes — F03.P1, F03.P2, F07.P1, F08.P2, F09.P1, F10.P1, F10.P2, F11.P1, F11.P2, F12.P2 and F14.P2 — previously had none, so the 'sole arbiter' question below was vacuously satisfied by anything that built and the probes' real demands lived in unnumbered prose. Remediation R-9 renumbered them; no probe's intent changed. OBSERVATION TARGET clauses are deliberately outside the numbering and are not read by this question.
deterministic_tie_break.named_substitution: Where a canonical_task explicitly names a substitution (F02.P2, F12.P1, F12.P2, F14.P1, F15.P1, F15.P2, F17.P2), writing the named substitute delivers some but not all numbered sub-requirements and is PARTIAL under P-a. It is never FULL and never NONE. See authoring rule R9.

evidence_required_per_pair: the fragment source text (or the NONE justification)
the exact build command and its exit status
the exact run command and the observed stdout/exit status against the canonical_task's stated result
the support level, the applicable P-letter(s) or N-reason, and a citation to the language documentation relied on
adjudication_and_audit.no_post_hoc_adjustment: Support levels are assigned from this rubric before any Q-metric aggregation and are not revised after coverage totals or rankings are seen (spec 6.1.7, 32).

interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule: PREDECLARED before any language beyond the Quidra and Python pilot fragments is measured, and before any metric has been computed on any language. Metrics A (Semantic Density), B (Semantic Determinacy), C (Semantic Locality) and D (Hidden Semantic Cost) are computed PRIMARILY on the COMMON BASIS — the set of probes for which ALL TEN languages have a fragment — so every language's Q is measured on identical material. The all-fragments basis is computed and published as a SECONDARY figure, together with each language's fragment count n_L and the delta between the two bases for every metric. Where the two bases disagree about a ranking, both rankings are published and the common basis is the one that is reported as the result.
interaction_with_quality_metrics.partial_fragments_enter_the_common_basis: YES. A probe is in the common basis if all ten languages have a fragment for it, whether that fragment is FULL or PARTIAL. Applied identically to all ten languages, with no exemption. Rationale: a PARTIAL fragment is a real fragment with real tokens, branches, lookups and hidden costs. Excluding PARTIALs from A-D while excluding NONEs as well would mean a language that can only approximate a probe pays for the clumsy approximation in A-D while a language that cannot do it at all pays nothing there — making PARTIAL sometimes worse for Q than NONE.
interaction_with_quality_metrics.why_this_replaced_the_variable_basis: The superseded rule computed A-D 'over the probes for which a fragment exists, i.e. probes scored FULL or PARTIAL for that language', so every language's Q was measured on a different probe basis, with no requirement to publish the basis size. The excluded NONE probes are exactly the token-heavy, lookup-heavy, hidden-cost-heavy ones (concurrency, FFI, deterministic destruction, closures, heap identity), so dropping them RAISES Q, and it raises it most for whichever language has the most NONEs. Spec 6.1.4 nowhere authorises a variable basis. This is an aggregation shape that changes a score through averaging rather than through measurement, and it is removed.
interaction_with_quality_metrics.capability_channel: Capability Coverage C, computed on the full fixed 88-point denominator, remains the SOLE channel through which unsupported capabilities affect the score. A probe scored NONE contributes 0 to the numerator and its full capability points to the denominator (NA-2).
interaction_with_quality_metrics.basis_reporting_requirement: Every published table of A, B, C or D must state, in the table, the basis used ('common' or 'all-fragments'), the size of that basis, and for the all-fragments basis each language's n_L. A figure published without its basis size is not a result.
interaction_with_quality_metrics.metric_E_denominator: Per spec 6.1.4.E, Capability Efficiency divides counted semantic-complexity units by the number of SUPPORTED capability points, i.e. sum over probes of capability_points * support_factor. This is the same numerator quantity used for Capability Coverage. Metric E's numerator is counted on the same basis as A-D and the basis is stated with the figure.
interaction_with_quality_metrics.anti_gaming_note: No claim is made here that any particular aggregation makes a trade 'unprofitable'. The superseded note asserted that the harmonic mean made it unprofitable for a language to raise Q by failing hard probes, but showed no derivation, and the assertion was false under a variable basis. The common basis removes the trade mechanically instead of arguing about it: a language cannot change the material its A-D are measured on, because that material is the same 44-probe intersection for everyone. Any residual sensitivity of the aggregate to basis choice is published as the common/all-fragments delta rather than asserted away.

support_rubric.determinacy_is_not_a_support_criterion: BINDING. Support level records ONLY whether the canonical_task's stated behavior is delivered. Whether a fact is recoverable from the local surface form is measured exclusively by metrics B (Semantic Determinacy) and D (Hidden Semantic Cost) and NEVER affects FULL/PARTIAL/NONE. A fragment that delivers the behavior while leaving facts locally indeterminate is FULL and pays for the indeterminacy in B and D. This applies identically to all ten languages: it is the rule that keeps a dynamically typed language from being charged twice for dynamic typing, and equally the rule that keeps a statically typed language from being credited twice for static typing.
support_rubric.observation_target_clauses: Clauses in a canonical_task prefixed 'OBSERVATION TARGET (not a support requirement; scored by metrics B/D only)' are NON-NORMATIVE for support scoring. They name what metrics B and D will look for in the fragment. They carry no number, they are not read by deterministic_tie_break, and a fragment that delivers every numbered sub-requirement is FULL whether or not a reader can recover the observation target from it. Eighteen probes carried such a clause unmarked before remediation R-3, with nothing stating whether it was a support requirement.

capability_coverage.formula: C = 100 * (sum over the 44 probes of capability_points * support_factor) / total_fixed_capability_points
capability_coverage.reporting_requirement: Report C in aggregate AND broken down by each of the 20 capability families, using capability_points_by_family as each family's denominator (spec 6.1.5). Report the per-family breakdown for all ten languages in the fixed column order, so that a family in which one language scores zero is visible rather than averaged away.
capability_coverage.denominator_derivation: 2 points per probe x 44 probes = 88. See capability_point_assignment_rule. The superseded denominator was 103 under an irreproducible per-probe vector of 1-3 points.

na_policy.note: Per spec section 26 and 6.1.1: for Semantic Compression Capability Coverage, an unsupported capability in this fixed universe REMAINS IN THE DENOMINATOR and therefore LOWERS coverage rather than becoming N/A. A missing capability must not escape scoring by being labeled N/A.
rules: NA-1. The denominator is fixed at 88 capability points for every one of the 10 languages, and is changed only by adding a probe under amendment_procedure before any measurement — never by any language's results, and never because a language lacks a capability.
NA-2. A probe scored NONE for a language contributes 0 to that language's numerator and its full capability_points to the denominator. It is NOT marked N/A and it is NOT excluded.
NA-3. No probe may be deleted, reworded, or re-weighted because a language (including Quidra) lacks the capability (spec 32).

NA-4. The only legitimate N/A in Primary Evaluation 1 would be a measurement that cannot be taken for a reason unrelated to the language's capability — e.g. a metric-A token count for a probe where no fragment exists. That is handled by the interaction_with_quality_metrics rule above (exclusion from A-D), NOT by removing the probe from coverage.
NA-5. Every N/A actually recorded anywhere in Primary Evaluation 1 must carry a written reason naming which of these rules permits it (spec 26 final line).

NA-6. 'The language has no concept of X' is a NONE with a written justification, never an N/A. This applies symmetrically to all ten languages, and the benchmark records it without commentary about which language is affected. No list of probes on which NONE is 'expected' is stated here: the superseded NA-6 named ten probes and predicted their outcome, which is a result embedded in a frozen instrument. Which probes yield NONE for which language is an output of the measurement, not an input to it.

hard_family_honesty_declaration.statement: The five families where the 10 languages differ most (concurrency, FFI, ownership/lifetime/destruction, alternatives/sum types, generics/polymorphism) are included at full weight and are NOT softened. They carry 24 of the 88 capability points (27.3%). Two of them, 14 and 15, were additionally widened by remediation so they are scored in BOTH directions rather than only in the direction a closed, statically resolved design wins: F14.P3 scores extension of an alternative set from a separate unit, and F15.P3 scores runtime dispatch through an abstract element type.
hard_family_honesty_declaration.expected_asymmetry_is_not_a_defect: It is expected and correct that some languages score NONE on several of these probes while others score FULL. That spread is the measurement, not a flaw in it. No probe in these families was weakened to reduce the spread, and none may be weakened afterwards.
hard_family_honesty_declaration.symmetry_check: Each of these families is scored by exactly the same rubric text and the same tie-break question as every other family. No family has a language-specific exemption, carve-out, or bonus. The symmetry test applied to every remediation in remediation_changelog was: would this rule look equally reasonable if Quidra were replaced by Zig, or by Python? Any rule that made sense only because of something the subject language specifically does or lacks was rewritten so that any of the ten languages could satisfy or fail it.

downstream_obligations.freeze_order: Per spec 6.1.7 the remaining items must be frozen before measurement and are the subject of sibling methodology documents: (3) the hidden-behavior checklist and metrics D/E (methodology/04_hidden_cost_and_capability_efficiency.md); (5) token-counting and normalization rules (methodology/02_fact_taxonomy_and_density.md), which authoring rule R10 now also relies on for fragment selection; metrics B and C (methodology/03_determinacy_and_locality.md); and (6) per-probe validation against each real implementation or authoritative specification, which is now gated by pre_measurement_validation V1-V5 in this file rather than deferred. Documents 02, 03 and 04 are all load-bearing for the Semantic Compression score and are named here because the superseded freeze_order listed only 02.
downstream_obligations.publication: Per spec 6.1.7, the probe definitions (this file), raw counts, scoring scripts, capability matrix, and normalization calculations must all be published in benchmark/. In addition, the pre_measurement_validation V1-V5 evidence, the R10 alternative-form records with their token counts and documentation citations, the common-basis and all-fragments figures with their basis sizes and per-language fragment counts, and the F11.P1.checked evidence-only variants must be published.

amendment_procedure.rule: Defects found by pre_measurement_validation, by adversarial audit, or by any reviewer BEFORE a score has been computed are corrected in place. Each correction receives a number and a date in methodology/CORRECTIONS.md, the superseded text is preserved verbatim there and in this file's remediation_changelog, and every measurement taken under the superseded text is re-taken.
amendment_procedure.prohibited: Any change made after a score has been observed; any change whose justification is that it improves (or worsens) a named language's position; any deletion or re-weighting of a capability because a language lacks it (spec 32, NA-3).
amendment_procedure.supersedes: This procedure supersedes the previous absolute freeze wording, which made it impossible to repair a defect that pre-measurement validation finds and contradicted spec 10.4's fix-and-record rule and this run's own CORRECTIONS.md practice.

no_results_observed_at_remediation: As of 2026-09-17, at the time the remediation recorded in remediation_changelog was applied, NO Semantic Compression score, sub-score, rank, or aggregate had been computed from this document or from any sibling methodology document for any of the ten languages. Only Quidra and Python probe fragments existed, and no metric had been run over them. Every change below is therefore pre-registration, not post-result formula selection (spec 32).
probes_per_family_note: Value 2 is the guaranteed MINIMUM per family (spec 6.1.2 floor), not a uniform count. Families 4, 5, 14 and 15 carry 3 probes after remediation R-1, R-4 and R-12, which added the counterpart probes those families were missing. See probes_per_family_by_family.

capability_point_assignment_rule.rule: Every probe is worth exactly 2 capability points. Each family's weight is therefore 2 x (number of probes in that family), and the denominator is 2 x probe_count = 88.
capability_point_assignment_rule.why_uniform: The previous vector assigned 1, 2 or 3 points per probe and 3 to 6 per family with no stated derivation, and no mechanical rule reproduces it: it is not the count of numbered sub-requirements (F01.P1 had 2 sub-requirements and 2 points; F01.P2 had 2 and 3 points) and it is not the count of semantic_facts_expected (F02.P1 had 5 facts and 3 points; F02.P2 had 5 facts and 2 points). An irreproducible weight vector is the single most load-bearing unaudited number in the document, because it is both the Capability Coverage denominator and metric E's denominator. A uniform vector is reproducible by inspection and is defensible without a derivation.
capability_point_assignment_rule.neutrality: Uniform weighting is decided by counting probes, not by looking at any language. Under the previous vector the two families in which all ten languages are equally capable (3 mutation and 7 arithmetic) carried the lowest weight, 3 points each; uniform weighting raises them to 4 and lowers nothing by name.
capability_point_assignment_rule.effect_on_the_hard_family_share: Recomputed and published rather than targeted: families 14, 15, 17, 19 and 20 now carry 24 of 88 points (27.3%) against 30 of 103 (29.1%) before. The change follows mechanically from removing an underivable vector and from adding counterpart probes to families 4, 5, 14 and 15; it was not chosen for its effect, and it is recorded here so a reader can see it.
capability_point_assignment_rule.frozen: This rule, not the numbers it produces, is what is frozen. Any future probe added under amendment_procedure is worth 2 points and raises the denominator by 2.

pre_measurement_validation._purpose: Spec 6.1.7 item 6 and spec 10.4 require each probe to be validated against the real implementation or authoritative specification, and require a mandatory pre-flight. The superseded document deferred all of this to downstream_obligations and carried no validation triad, so every NONE this instrument produced was indistinguishable from a probe that is simply unwritable as specified. These gates must be satisfied, and their evidence preserved, BEFORE any language beyond the pilot is scored.
pre_measurement_validation.V1_fragments_build_and_match: Every fragment scored FULL or PARTIAL builds and runs under its frozen recipe, unmodified, and its observed output matches the canonical_task's stated result. This was already implied by authoring rule R6; it is now an explicit gate, and the build command, exit status and observed stdout are preserved as evidence for every (probe, language) pair.
pre_measurement_validation.V2_validators_and_harness_conventions: Every mechanical validator the probe set defines is exercised on a known-positive AND a known-negative case before it is trusted, and both outcomes are recorded. Specifically, F20.P2's `nm` check is run once on a binary known to export `add2` and once on a binary known not to, and both outcomes are recorded; a validator that can never fail, or never pass, would otherwise produce NONE rows silently. Separately, every harness convention a canonical_task withholds — Java's `Main` class name, file naming, package directories, entry wrappers, the async runtime block F19.P1 permits — is satisfied by the harness and is NEVER charged to the fragment as tokens, as a P-e PARTIAL, or as a NONE.
pre_measurement_validation.V3_every_probe_expressible_somewhere: Every probe is demonstrated expressible at FULL in at least one of the ten languages, with the working fragment recorded, BEFORE any language is scored NONE against that probe. A probe no language can satisfy is an instrument defect, not a finding about the languages.
pre_measurement_validation.V4_suspicious_rows_and_columns: Any probe with ten NONEs, and any language with NONE on more than a third of the probes, is investigated as a SUSPECTED INSTRUMENT DEFECT before the row or column is reported as a result. The investigation, its conclusion and the evidence are recorded in CORRECTIONS.md whether or not a defect is found. This gate applies identically to all ten languages, including the subject language: a surprisingly LOW column and a surprisingly HIGH column are both investigated.
pre_measurement_validation.V5_recipe_agreement: toolchain_binding.recipes is checked for exact agreement with environment/environment.json -> frozen_toolchain_recipes under the name mapping in toolchain_binding.recipes_authority, and the check is recorded. A disagreement between the two frozen copies is an instrument defect that blocks measurement. Until the counterpart change listed in counterpart_obligations is applied to environment.json, this gate FAILS by construction and no fragment may be built.
pre_measurement_validation.evidence_is_preserved: The outputs of V1-V5 are published in benchmark/ alongside the probe definitions and raw counts, per spec 6.1.7.

counterpart_obligations._purpose: Cross-document contradictions named by the audit are fixed on THIS side as the finding specified. The matching change each sibling document's owner must make is recorded here so it is not lost. Until every obligation below is discharged, pre_measurement_validation V5 fails and no measurement may be taken.

obligations.change_required: Set rust.build to `rustc -O -C debug-assertions=on FILE.rs -o BIN`, zig.build to `zig build-exe -OReleaseSafe FILE.zig -femit-bin=BIN`, and typescript.build to `tsc --strict --target es2022 --module nodenext FILE.ts`, matching this file byte for byte. Add the safety_mode_clause rationale, or reference it here, so the `_policy` line 'every language uses its normal optimized/release build' is not read as authorising an unchecked mode for some languages and a checked mode for others.
obligations.why: Findings 2 and 10. `rustc -O` alone turns debug assertions off, so `+` wraps rather than panicking, and `-OReleaseFast` makes Zig's signed overflow and out-of-bounds indexing undefined behavior, while the evaluated Quidra build has only an optimized-and-checked mode. Probes F08.P1, F08.P2 and F11.P1 score exactly that difference. Non-strict `tsc` erases the optionality F12.P1 and F12.P2 measure.

obligations.change_required: Add the multi-unit build commands for F18.P2 and F14.P3 exactly as frozen in toolchain_binding.multi_unit_recipes, and record that they are not a P-b deviation.
obligations.why: Finding 8. `clang++ ... FILE.cpp` and `go build -o BIN FILE.go` compile one unit, so C++ and Go would be scored down on a visibility-boundary probe for a harness limitation, which spec 10.4 forbids.

obligations.change_required: Confirm that B and C are computed on the COMMON BASIS as primary with the all-fragments basis as a published secondary, that PARTIAL fragments are included, and that every published figure states its basis and basis size. Confirm that B is the sole home of local determinacy, since rubric criterion F-5 has been deleted here.
obligations.why: Findings 3 and 6. Determinacy must be counted once, in B/D, and A-D must be measured on identical material for all ten languages.

obligations.change_required: Confirm the same common-basis rule for D, and update metric E's denominator reference from 103 to 88 supported-capability points with the 2-points-per-probe rule.
obligations.why: Findings 5 and 6. The capability-point vector changed, and E divides by supported capability points.

obligations.change_required: No change to the tokenizer is required, but authoring rule R10 now makes the tokenizer load-bearing for FRAGMENT SELECTION as well as for metric A. Confirm the tokenizer is available and frozen before any fragment is authored.
obligations.why: Finding 7. R10 selects the fragment text by token count, which is what actually moves metrics A-D.

obligations.change_required: Record the remediation entries in remediation_changelog below as numbered, dated defect entries with the superseded text preserved verbatim, in the same form as D-1 through D-4.
obligations.why: Finding 15b and spec 10.4: defects found during a run are fixed and recorded, not silently corrected.

obligations.change_required: The Quidra and Python fragments for F04.P1, F04.P2, F05.P2, F09.P2, F12.P2 and F15.P1 must be re-authored against the remediated canonical_tasks (renamed identifiers, changed constants, descending sort, locally declared `h`), and fragments must be authored for the four new probes F04.P3, F05.P3, F14.P3 and F15.P3. No measurement has been taken from the old fragments.

remediation_changelog._purpose: Record of the adversarial-audit remediation applied to this document on 2026-09-17. Each entry states the finding's severity, the defect in one line, what changed, and — for every Quidra-bias finding — which direction the correction is expected to move Quidra's score.
remediation_changelog.no_results_observed: NO score, sub-score, rank or aggregate had been computed from this document or any sibling methodology document for any of the ten languages when these changes were made. Only Quidra and Python probe fragments existed and no metric had been run over them. This remediation is therefore legitimate pre-registration, not post-result formula selection (spec 32).
remediation_changelog.symmetry_test_applied: Every change was checked against: would this rule look equally reasonable if Quidra were replaced by Zig, or by Python? Rules that made sense only because of something the subject language specifically does or lacks were rewritten so that any of the ten languages could satisfy or fail them. No compensating bias in the opposite direction was introduced: each added probe scores a capability that at least six of the ten comparison languages provide as a first-class standard feature, under the same rubric text and the same tie-break question as every existing probe.
remediation_changelog.net_expected_direction: LOWER for Quidra. The dominant effects are R-1 and R-4, which add four counterpart probes (8 of 88 points) covering function/closure values, heap object identity, extension of an alternative set from a separate unit, and runtime dispatch through an abstract element type — capabilities the subject language's own documentation says it does not provide, and which were previously worth 0 of 103 points. R-2 removes an unchecked-mode advantage the frozen recipes gave Rust and Zig on the three probes that score overflow and bounds behavior, R-3 stops charging dynamically typed languages twice for dynamic typing, R-6 stops NONE-heavy languages from raising Q by having fewer fragments, and R-10 gives TypeScript the optionality it actually has. Each of these raises a comparison language relative to Quidra. One change, R-5's uniform weight vector, incidentally lowers the combined share of the five hardest families from 29.1%% to 27.3%%; that share is published rather than targeted, it follows mechanically from removing an underivable vector, and it is small against the 8 points added by R-1 and R-4.

entries.finding: Finding 1 — no probe requires constructing or passing a function value
entries.defect: The one construct the subject language cannot express and the other nine can — a first-class function or closure value — was worth 0 of 103 points, and three probes routed around it: F12.P2 supplied `h` as given context, F09.P2 excused a comparator 'if the language supplies a default order', and F16.P1 permitted a plain loop instead of a fold.
entries.change: Added F05.P3 (2 points): declare a unary function value `neg` inside the measured fragment that captures an enclosing local `k`, pass it BY NAME at the argument position of the standard higher-order sequence operation (or of ordinary iteration where the standard library has none, so that a language without a stdlib `map` is not penalised for the wrong thing), and produce element 0. Deleted F09.P2's escape clause and made it require an EXPLICITLY supplied descending ordering, never the facility's default. Changed F12.P2 so `h` is declared inside the measured fragment. F16.P1's either/or is resolved by R10 (see R-7).
entries.quidra_score_direction: LOWER — expected NONE for Quidra on F05.P3 and a harder F09.P2/F12.P2; this is the measurement, not a defect, exactly as hard_family_honesty_declaration already accepts for concurrency and FFI.

entries.defect: The frozen recipes put Rust (`rustc -O`, debug assertions off) and Zig (`-OReleaseFast`, signed overflow and out-of-bounds indexing undefined) in their UNCHECKED configuration while Quidra and Swift were checked, and F08.P1, F08.P2 and F11.P1 score precisely that difference. F08.P1's demand that the overflow outcome be statable 'without consulting the build recipe' was unanswerable for Rust and Zig only because of the recipe this document froze.
entries.change: Rust recipe changed to `rustc -O -C debug-assertions=on FILE.rs -o BIN`, Zig to `zig build-exe -OReleaseSafe FILE.zig -femit-bin=BIN`. Added toolchain_binding.safety_mode_clause pinning the SAFETY POSTURE rather than the optimization level, recorded per language as a controlled variable, with C++ recorded as having no checked mode — a language fact scored by metrics B and D, not by the recipe. Added to P-b that the checked mode IS the frozen recipe and is not a deviation.
entries.quidra_score_direction: LOWER — Rust and Zig can now express locally determinate checked arithmetic and bounds behavior on F08.P1, F08.P2 and F11.P1, closing an advantage the recipe had handed the subject language.

entries.finding: Finding 3 — determinacy double-counted in coverage and in metrics B/D
entries.defect: Support rubric criterion F-5 required every expected fact kind to be DETERMINABLE, with no bound on the permitted analysis, so a dynamically typed language could be pushed to PARTIAL on many probes purely for being dynamic — paying once in B/D and again in C, which enters the harmonic mean. Separately, 18 canonical_tasks ended with an unnumbered 'A reader must be able to determine X' clause and nothing said whether those clauses were support requirements.
entries.change: Deleted criterion F-5 (slot retained so cross-references to F-6 still resolve). Added the binding rule support_rubric.determinacy_is_not_a_support_criterion: support records only whether the stated behavior is delivered, and local recoverability is measured exclusively by B and D. Prefixed every affected clause in F01.P2, F04.P2, F06.P1, F07.P2, F08.P1, F09.P1, F09.P2, F10.P1, F10.P2, F11.P1, F11.P2, F13.P1, F13.P2, F14.P2, F16.P2, F17.P1, F18.P1 and F20.P1 with 'OBSERVATION TARGET (not a support requirement; scored by metrics B/D only):', and added support_rubric.observation_target_clauses making them non-normative.
entries.superseded_text: F-5. Every fact kind listed in semantic_facts_expected is DETERMINABLE for that language at the probe (possibly requiring non-local lookup — locality cost is metric C's business, not coverage's).
entries.quidra_score_direction: LOWER — Python and TypeScript stop paying a coverage penalty on top of the determinacy penalty they already pay in B and D, which raises them relative to Quidra.

entries.finding: Finding 4 — false Quidra-independence claim, and four probes shaped by Quidra's README
entries.defect: provenance_and_fairness_statement.derivation asserted that no Quidra documentation or example was consulted and no probe was shaped by its feature set. F15.P1 (`first`, generic T, `values[0]`), F05.P2 (`g(int &value)`, value 7, caller local initialized to 1), F04.P1 (`x` = 1 plus a second name for the same storage) and F04.P2 (non-copying read-only view) reproduce Quidra's own README examples for its design laws 1, 2 and 3, carrying 12 of 103 points.
entries.change: Replaced the derivation paragraph with a truthful one that withdraws the claim and lists the pairings. Rewrote identifiers and constants off the README's: F04.P1 `x`/1/`r`/9 -> `slot`/4/`port`/9; F04.P2 `v` -> `window`; F05.P2 `g`/`x`/1/7 -> `put`/`cell`/3/12; F15.P1 `first`/1,2,3/"x","y" -> `head`/4,5,6/"p","q". Added a counterpart probe to each affected family, chosen to exercise the capability a value-semantics-with-explicit-storage design excludes: F04.P3 (two independently obtained handles observed to denote the same heap object, using a standard reference-identity operation), F05.P3 (see R-1), F14.P3 (see R-12) and F15.P3 (heterogeneous sequence behind one abstract element type, dispatched at runtime). Each is scored by the same rubric and tie-break question as every other probe.
entries.superseded_text: Every probe in this file was derived exclusively from (a) the 20 capability families enumerated verbatim in spec section 6.1.2, (b) the semantic-fact inventory in spec section 6.1.3, and (c) general programming-language theory. No Quidra documentation, source, examples, README, or grammar was consulted. No probe was shaped by Quidra's operators, types, syntax, keywords, or feature set.
entries.quidra_score_direction: LOWER — the four families that previously asked only the sub-question Quidra's design laws exist to answer now ask the dual question too, and Quidra is expected to score NONE on the counterparts.

entries.finding: Finding 5 — the 103-point weight vector has no derivation rule
entries.defect: Per-probe values ranged 1 to 3 and per-family totals 3 to 6 with no stated basis, and no mechanical rule reproduces them: not the count of numbered sub-requirements (F01.P1 had 2 and 2 points; F01.P2 had 2 and 3), not the count of semantic_facts_expected (F02.P1 had 5 facts and 3 points; F02.P2 had 5 and 2). The vector is both the Capability Coverage denominator and metric E's denominator.
entries.change: Replaced with a uniform vector: every probe is worth 2 points, each family weighs 2 x (its probe count), and the denominator is 2 x 44 = 88. Added capability_point_assignment_rule stating the rule, why uniform was chosen over a reconstructed derivation, and the recomputed hard-family share. Updated capability_coverage, capability_points_by_family, NA-1 and metric E's denominator reference.
entries.quidra_score_direction: MIXED, small. Uniform weighting raises the two families in which all ten languages are equally capable (3 mutation, 7 arithmetic) from 3 points to 4, and lowers the combined share of the five hardest families from 29.1% to 27.3% — which, taken alone, would slightly HELP a language that fails hard probes. That effect is published rather than hidden, follows mechanically from removing an underivable vector, and is small against the 8 points R-1 and R-4 added in exactly those families' direction.

entries.finding: Finding 6 — metrics A-D computed on a per-language variable basis
entries.defect: A-D were computed only over each language's FULL-or-PARTIAL probes, so every language's Q was measured on different material with no requirement to publish the basis size. The excluded NONE probes are the token-heavy, lookup-heavy, hidden-cost-heavy ones, so dropping them raises Q most for whichever language has the most NONEs. PARTIAL fragments were kept in A-D, so approximating a probe could cost more in Q than not doing it at all. The anti_gaming_note asserted the harmonic mean made this unprofitable but showed no derivation.
entries.change: Replaced interaction_with_quality_metrics with a predeclared COMMON BASIS rule: A-D are computed primarily on the set of probes for which all ten languages have a fragment, so every language's Q is measured on identical material; the all-fragments basis is published as a secondary figure with each language's n_L and the delta; PARTIAL fragments DO enter the common basis, applied identically to all ten languages; every published figure must state its basis and basis size; Capability Coverage on the fixed 88-point denominator remains the sole channel through which unsupported capabilities affect the score. Replaced the unproved anti-gaming assertion with the mechanical statement.
entries.quidra_score_direction: LOWER — a language with more NONEs no longer gains a higher Q from a smaller, easier basis, and this is expected to affect the youngest language most.

entries.finding: Finding 7 — 'the way a normal author would write it' is an undefined judgement that moves every metric
entries.defect: R2 and its restatements inside canonical_tasks selected the fragment text from which A, B, C and D are all computed, with no tie-break. F16.P1 openly permitted either an explicit loop or a standard sum, a ~5x token difference in Python on a probe that feeds Semantic Density directly. deterministic_tie_break arbitrated only the support LEVEL, never the TEXT.
entries.change: Added authoring rule R10_deterministic_form_selection: fewest tokens under methodology 02's frozen tokenizer, ties broken by first appearance in the language's official documentation, every alternative considered recorded with its token count and citation. A canonical_task's own explicit preference order overrides R10. Removed the either/or from F16.P1 and F16.P2 and routed F03.P1, F07.P2, F09.P1, F09.P2, F10.P2, F11.P1, F11.P2 and F14.P2 through R10. Updated R2 to defer to R10 and noted the tie-break's new scope.
entries.quidra_score_direction: UNCHANGED in direction — R10 is a mechanical rule applied identically to all ten languages; it removes an author's degree of freedom rather than moving any language.

entries.finding: Finding 8 — F18.P2 requires a second unit that two frozen recipes cannot build
entries.defect: F18.P2 declared a second file permitted, but `clang++ ... FILE.cpp -o BIN` compiles one translation unit and `go build -o BIN FILE.go` compiles one named file while Go's lowercase-is-package-scoped rule needs a separate package. C++ and Go would have been scored down for a harness limitation — the failure mode spec 10.4 forbids — while the subject language's single-command module reference took FULL.
entries.change: Added toolchain_binding.multi_unit_recipes naming the exact augmented command per language for F18.P2 and the new F14.P3 (C++ `clang++ -std=c++20 -O2 util.cpp FILE.cpp -o BIN`; Go `go build -o BIN ./...` with go.mod and a util/ package; Swift, Java and Kotlin likewise; Rust, TypeScript, Zig, Python and Quidra unchanged), declared it not a P-b deviation, and added the spec-10.4 rule that any language forced to PARTIAL or NONE solely by the single-file recipe must be re-run before the result is reported. Updated P-e's exemption list and F18.P2's own text.
entries.quidra_score_direction: LOWER — C++ and Go recover a 2-point probe they would have lost to the harness rather than to their languages.

entries.finding: Finding 9 — eleven probes had no numbered sub-requirements, so the 'sole arbiter' arbitrated nothing
entries.defect: deterministic_tie_break asks whether the fragment delivers every explicitly numbered sub-requirement. F03.P1, F03.P2, F07.P1, F08.P2, F09.P1, F10.P1, F10.P2, F11.P1, F11.P2, F12.P2 and F14.P2 had none, so the question was vacuously satisfied by anything that built while the real demands lived in unnumbered prose — a Python `e = xs[i]` that raises IndexError delivered all zero of F11.P1's numbered sub-requirements.
entries.change: Renumbered all eleven canonical_tasks so every behavioral demand carries its own (1)/(2)/(3), with OBSERVATION TARGET clauses deliberately left outside the numbering. Added deterministic_tie_break.numbering_guarantee recording that all 44 tasks are now numbered and that no probe's intent changed, and deterministic_tie_break.named_substitution fixing the level for the seven probes that name a substitution.
entries.quidra_score_direction: UNCHANGED in direction — the arbiter now arbitrates for every language equally; it removes reviewer disagreement rather than moving a score.

entries.finding: Finding 10 — the frozen TypeScript recipe runs non-strict
entries.defect: `tsc FILE.ts` with no tsconfig and no flags leaves `strict` and `strictNullChecks` off, so `let o: number | undefined = undefined; let n: number = o;` compiles clean, erasing the point of F12.P1 and F12.P2 for TypeScript. The rubric then trapped the language: enabling `--strict` was a flag beyond the frozen recipe under P-b and forced PARTIAL.
entries.change: Changed the frozen TypeScript recipe to `tsc --strict --target es2022 --module nodenext FILE.ts` and added toolchain_binding.typescript_strict_clause declaring `--strict` part of the recipe, not a P-b deviation, because non-strict is not production-reasonable under R2 or spec 7. Recorded the matching environment.json change as a counterpart obligation.
entries.quidra_score_direction: LOWER — TypeScript is credited with the type-level optionality it actually has, on two probes where it was previously credited with none.

entries.finding: Finding 11 — F08.P1 named no preference order among explicit overflow operations
entries.defect: F08.P1 said to use 'the one that makes the behavior explicit at the site' where several exist. Rust offers checked_add, wrapping_add, saturating_add and overflowing_add; Zig offers +%, +| and @addWithOverflow; Swift offers &+ and addingReportingOverflow. The four differ in token count (A), surviving interpretations (B) and whether a failure path appears (D), so an unstated choice moved three metrics. F08.P2 in the same family already supplied an explicit (i)/(ii)/(iii) order.
entries.change: Gave F08.P1 the same shape: (i) standard checked operation yielding an optional/error value with 0 substituted for the exceptional case; (ii) standard wrapping; (iii) standard saturating; (iv) the plain operator — recording which rung was used and why each higher rung was unavailable. Applied the same rung-and-record form to F10.P1's conversion preference, and replaced F08.P2's 'if neither is idiomatic' with 'if neither is available in that language's standard library'.
entries.quidra_score_direction: UNCHANGED in direction — one fixed order applied identically to every language that has the operations.

entries.finding: Finding 12 — family 14 rewards closedness and nothing rewards extensibility
entries.defect: F14.P1 demanded that the language's own rules prevent a third alternative being added and routed open class hierarchies to PARTIAL; F14.P2 forbade a default arm and scored exhaustiveness. The dual capability — adding a new alternative from a separate compilation unit without editing the original, the point of open polymorphism in Java, Kotlin, Swift, C++, Python and TypeScript — was worth zero points anywhere in the universe. The family was scored in one direction only.
entries.change: Added F14.P3 (2 points), the exact mirror of F14.P1: declare an abstract `area` over shapes in a unit `shapes`; from a SEPARATE unit that does not modify `shapes`, introduce a third shape `Tri` implementing `area`; call `area` through a value of the abstract type holding a `Tri`. A language whose rules prevent extension from outside the declaring unit records NONE with the citation. Its second unit is covered by multi_unit_recipes and is exempt from P-e. Added notes to F14.P1 and F14.P3 that closedness and extensibility are scored separately and neither result implies the other.
entries.quidra_score_direction: LOWER — expected NONE for Quidra, whose documentation states there is no implicit runtime subtype relation, no implicit upcast and no hidden dynamic dispatch, on a probe six comparison languages satisfy as a matter of course.

entries.finding: Finding 13 — no pre-measurement validation, so every NONE is indistinguishable from an unwritable probe
entries.defect: The document declared itself frozen while deferring all probe validation downstream and carried no analogue of spec 10.4's validation triad: the F20.P2 `nm` validator was never required to be exercised on a known-positive and a known-negative case, no rule required an all-NONE row or column to be investigated as an instrument defect, and no rule required a probe to be shown expressible somewhere before any language was scored NONE against it.
entries.change: Added pre_measurement_validation with V1 (every FULL/PARTIAL fragment builds, runs and matches the stated result, evidence preserved), V2 (every mechanical validator exercised on a known-positive and a known-negative case with both outcomes recorded; withheld harness conventions — Java's `Main`, file naming, package directories, entry wrappers — satisfied by the harness and never charged to the fragment), V3 (every probe demonstrated expressible at FULL in at least one language before any NONE is recorded), V4 (any probe with ten NONEs, or any language with NONE on more than a third of the probes, investigated as a suspected instrument defect, with surprisingly HIGH columns investigated on the same footing as surprisingly low ones) and V5 (the two frozen recipe copies checked for agreement).
entries.quidra_score_direction: UNCHANGED in direction — a gate applied identically in both directions to all ten languages.

entries.finding: Finding 14 — F19.P2's no-synchronization clause invites a factually wrong FULL
entries.defect: The clause let a language whose semantics 'make this program race-free WITHOUT any explicit synchronization construct (e.g. a global interpreter lock...)' write the unsynchronized fragment. A GIL does not make `counter += 1` atomic — it is a read-modify-write across bytecodes — and Python 3.14, the frozen version, ships a free-threaded build. An analyst following it literally would credit capability points to a program with a data race on the strength of one lucky run.
entries.change: Tightened the clause: the unsynchronized form is permitted ONLY if the language's own documentation states a NORMATIVE guarantee that the specific read-modify-write in (2) is atomic, with the sentence quoted and cited in the evidence record; an interpreter-wide lock that serializes bytecodes without making a read-modify-write atomic does NOT satisfy this and the fragment must use an explicit synchronization construct. Verification requires the value 2000 on 20 consecutive runs, all 20 outcomes recorded, with any other value a failed verification.
entries.quidra_score_direction: HIGHER, marginally, relative to Python — Python must now write the explicit synchronization construct, which costs it tokens in metric A. This correction moves the benchmark toward Quidra on one probe and is applied anyway, because the superseded clause would have recorded a factually false capability (spec 4: if a value cannot be measured honestly, do not fabricate it).

entries.finding: Finding 15 — R9 contradicted seven probes, the freeze wording forbade repairing a defect, and NA-6 pre-announced results
entries.defect: (a) R9 said never substitute an easier task, while F02.P2, F12.P1, F12.P2, F14.P1, F15.P1, F15.P2 and F17.P2 each explicitly instructed substitution. (b) `status` forbade any probe ever being reworded and no_post_hoc_redesign said a discovered defect is recorded as an erratum 'not silently repaired here', making it impossible to repair a defect pre-measurement validation finds — contradicting spec 10.4 and this run's own CORRECTIONS.md, which does exactly that for methodology 02. (c) NA-6 pre-announced NONE as 'the expected outcome for several languages' on ten named probes.
entries.change: (a) Amended R9 with the named-substitution exception: write the named substitute and score PARTIAL under P-a, never FULL, and made the seven probes say 'score PARTIAL under P-a' instead of 'score by the rubric'. Added deterministic_tie_break.named_substitution. (b) Replaced the freeze wording with amendment_procedure: pre-measurement defects are corrected, numbered and dated in CORRECTIONS.md with the superseded text preserved verbatim and affected measurements re-taken; only changes made after results are observed, or made to improve a language's position, are prohibited. (c) Deleted the ten-probe expectation list from NA-6, keeping only the rule that 'the language has no concept of X' is a NONE and never an N/A.
entries.quidra_score_direction: UNCHANGED in direction — removes contradictions and a predicted result; no language's position changes.

entries.finding: Finding 16 — four loose ends that would be argued about later
entries.defect: (a) F11.P1's `.checked` variant was 'measured and reported separately' but no metric consumed it and nothing forbade citing it selectively after results. (b) F20.P2 made `nm` evidence mandatory including for NONE, but Python and TypeScript produce no compiled artifact, so the required evidence could not exist. (c) toolchain_binding.recipes duplicated environment.json verbatim with no checksum and already differed in shape (one Quidra entry here, quidra_native/quidra_interpreter there). (d) freeze_order named only sibling documents 02, omitting 03 (metrics B and C) and 04 (metrics D and E).
entries.change: (a) Added to F11.P1 that the `.checked` variant enters no metric, is evidence only, may not be substituted in any calculation of A-E, and changes neither the capability points nor the support level. (b) Added to F20.P2 and to the NONE criteria that a language with no compiled artifact records N-1 with the nm field reading 'no compiled artifact under the frozen recipe' — a NONE, not an N/A under NA-5. (c) Added toolchain_binding.recipes_authority naming environment.json as the single authority with the name mapping, plus validation gate V5 requiring the two copies to be checked for agreement before measurement. (d) Extended freeze_order to name 02, 03 and 04 and to record that validation is now gated in this file rather than deferred.

entries.finding: Finding 17 — rubric criterion F-6 disqualified mechanisms on an unobservable test
entries.defect: F-6 disqualified a mechanism the documentation marks 'unsafe, deprecated, discouraged, or reflective'. 'Discouraged' and 'reflective' have no observable test, and the carve-out rescued only facilities gated behind an unsafe/unchecked keyword — leaving Python's `ctypes` (needed for F20.P1), Go's `unsafe`, Java's reflective access paths and C++'s raw-`new` guidance in the gap, so two reviewers could disagree about a probe on the basis of tone in a manual.
entries.change: Replaced the wording with an observable test: an explicit NORMATIVE prohibition or deprecation for ordinary use in the official reference or standard-library documentation, evidenced by a sentence containing 'deprecated', 'should not be used', 'do not use', 'must not be used', 'unstable', 'internal', 'no compatibility guarantee' or an equivalent normative form, with the exact sentence and URL quoted in the evidence record — absent the quotation the criterion is satisfied. Documented warnings about consequences of misuse ('can crash the interpreter') are explicitly not prohibitions.
entries.quidra_score_direction: LOWER — Python's `ctypes` and Go's `unsafe` can no longer be disqualified on tone, so those languages keep FFI points they might have lost.
